records.name: Roberto Martinez Foundation
records.summary: A nonprofit that gives scholarships, grants and help with basic needs to people on low to moderate incomes around Philadelphia. It also runs yearly golf, gala and party fundraisers, and volunteers help with those events and with community outreach.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer at the yearly events or with community outreach, or buy tickets to the golf, gala and party events.

schedule.text: Annual golf invitational, gala, and Blue and Gold events. The site does not give dates for them.

locations.label: Registered office (from the IRS record, not shown on the group's site)

cost.text: Tickets are sold for the yearly events. Prices are not shown on the site.

first_step.how: Use the contact form on rmfnd.com and choose Be a Volunteer to ask about the next event.
first_step.basis: Volunteering and public event tickets both have a clear way in, but the site does not say what a new volunteer does first.

records.notes: The homepage lists Blue and Gold Week for June 18 to July 1, 2027. That is a future date, so it is not used as a sign of life, and no past dated item was found, so last_sign_of_life is left out. The site has no accessibility statement. The foundation funds other groups, but it runs its own volunteer roles and public events, so it stays published.

records.name: Rock to the Future
records.summary: A free music program for young people in under-resourced parts of Philadelphia, run in schools, community centers and the juvenile justice system, with mentoring and college and career help.
records.what_you_do: Join a free music program such as Lyric Lab, a songwriting class for teens that builds toward a live performance. Volunteers and donors can also help.

schedule.text: Lyric Lab meets Mondays from 4 to 6 pm at One Art Community Center, and Concert Creators meets Thursdays from 4 to 6 pm at the same site. Music Production meets Mondays from 6 to 7:30 pm at a second site. The two MusiCore after-school programs meet at schools until 6 pm: Kensington on Mondays and Wednesdays, and Germantown on Tuesdays and Thursdays.

locations.label: As I Plant This Seed (Music Production)

cost.text: Free. Meals, transit passes, and instruments or supplies are provided.

first_step.how: Use the Sign Up Today form on the Join Now page for Lyric Lab or another program, or call 215-302-9633.
first_step.basis: The join page says beginners are welcome, supplies and instruments are provided, and each program has a Sign Up Today form. The MusiCore spots at the two schools are limited to their own students for now, with a waitlist for others.
first_step.what_to_expect: Lyric Lab meets Mondays from 4 to 6 pm at One Art Community Center for teens aged 13 to 19. Beginners are welcome, and students write original music together toward a performance. Meals, transit passes, and instruments are provided at no cost. After you send the interest form, a team member follows up.
first_visit_tips: Fill in the interest form on the join page before you come, since a team member follows up after it.
Check the age range: Lyric Lab and Music Production list ages 13 to 19, and MusiCore lists grades 6 to 12.
If you are not from Kensington High School or Roosevelt Elementary, join the MusiCore waitlist through the interest form.
If you want to volunteer, you can attend an orientation before your background checks are finished.

records.notes: Clearances apply to volunteers who work with students. Student participants do not need them. The volunteer page says clearances must be current within 5 years. The join page gives ZIP 19140 for the Lyric Lab address and 19131 for Concert Creators at the same street address, so the ZIP is left out. Named partner Face to Face (blog) and the As I Plant This Seed program site are listed as leads.

records.name: Ronnie Vega Memorial People's Fridge at LAVA
records.summary: A food pantry at LAVA on Lancaster Avenue in West Philadelphia, stocked with leftovers and neighbor donations. LAVA also holds a free market on the second Saturday of each month.
records.what_you_do: Take food at the Monday food share or the Thursday food distro, or come to the second Saturday free market.

schedule.text: LAVA lists a food share on Mondays from 3 to 5 pm, a food distro on Thursdays from 3 to 4 pm, and a Really Really Free Market on the second Saturday from 9 am to noon, all at 4134 Lancaster Ave.

first_step.how: Come to LAVA at 4134 Lancaster Ave during a posted food time, such as the Monday food share from 3 to 5 pm or the Thursday food distro from 3 to 4 pm. The site lists no sign-up.
first_step.basis: The site lists posted food times and describes the fridge as serving neighbors, with no eligibility rules or sign-up. It does not say which posted hours are the fridge's own, so check the Instagram page if you are unsure.
first_step.what_to_expect: The posted food times are on Monday afternoons (food share) and Thursday afternoons (food distro), and the free market is on the second Saturday morning. The stock comes from leftovers from the food distro, other food shares, and neighbor donations. The site does not say what to bring or how visits run.
first_visit_tips: Come during the posted food times, since the site lists no other hours.
The site does not say what to bring, so ask on the fridge's Instagram page before you go if you need to know.

records.notes: LAVA lists the food share, food distro, and free market as its own open hours. The site does not say which of them are the fridge's own, so the schedule says LAVA lists them. The LAVA programs page lists the fridge by name only, with no hours or sign-up. The LAVA updates page has nothing newer than May 2022, and the events page has no dated entries. The 2025 article is the newest dated evidence, more than 12 months old, so the status is probably_active. The WRC Community Food Share is also listed on the LAVA programs page, with no days shown, and is recorded as a lead.

records.name: Rose Pedals to Success
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that helps young people learn business skills, build leadership, and work toward money independence through cohort sessions and mentoring.
records.what_you_do: Young people sign up for cohort sessions, get mentoring, and get hands-on business practice. Families can also come to the group's Community Day family event.

schedule.text: Youth cohort sessions, with dates not published on the site. The office is open Monday to Friday, 9 am to 5 pm.

cost.text: Cohort sessions are free. The site does not state costs for other events.

first_step.how: Use the Sign Youth Up link on rosepedalstosuccess.org, or email info@rosepedalstosuccess.org to ask about the next cohort.
first_step.basis: A sign-up link and an email address are published, but the site does not state ages, neighborhoods, or how places are chosen.

records.notes: The site gives no cohort dates, ages, neighborhoods, session length, or format. The sign-up page did not show its form details when read, and the programs page returned not found. The About page names Marie Rose as founder and leader and names partners, but has no cohort details. The contact name Shanice Porter comes from the IRS and NCCS records. The August 23, 2026 Community Day is a one-time event and is kept only as the sign of life. Named partners Project HOME, Community First Fund, Mercy Vocational and Tech High School, Truist Bank, and the American Heart Association are listed as leads. The last two are large organizations and are unlikely to be community groups.

records.name: Rosenbach Museum & Library
records.summary: A museum and library at 2008 to 2010 Delancey Place that keeps rare books and manuscripts, open for study and for visits to its galleries and programs.
records.what_you_do: Visit the museum and its Treasures Gallery, join a course or public program, or ask about volunteering. Researchers can book appointments to study the collections.

schedule.text: Open Thursday to Saturday 10:30 am to 6 pm and Sunday 10:30 am to 4:30 pm. Closed Monday to Wednesday. Research visits follow different hours and need an appointment.

cost.text: Guided tour: adults $20, seniors $13, students with ID $10, ages 12 to 17 $10. Self-guided: adults $15, seniors $10, students $7.50, ages 12 to 17 $7.50. Children under 12, Rosenbach members, and AAM, ICOM and NARM members get in free.

access.notes: The south entrance is wheelchair accessible. Call 215-732-1600 ext. 110 before you arrive, and staff will meet you at the door. Service animals are welcome in public areas. Bathrooms are on the first floor, and lockers are available. A paid personal care attendant can come at no cost if you request a free attendant ticket in advance at rsvp@rosenbach.org.

first_step.how: Book a guided or self-guided visit online or by phone at 215-732-1600.
first_step.basis: Open to the public on posted hours with clear booking links, and several public events are free. The volunteer guide route needs an application, so it is not counted in the rating.
first_step.what_to_expect: Visits run during posted hours, Thursday to Sunday, and guided tours need a booking because space is limited. Self-guided visits use timed entry tickets and the free Bloomberg Connects app, so bring headphones. Photos and notes are welcome, but notes on paper must be in pencil, and video is not allowed during Signature Programs.
first_visit_tips: Book ahead online, by email, or by phone, since guided tour space is limited.
Bring headphones for the self-guided tour, which uses the free Bloomberg Connects app.
Use a pencil for any notes on paper, and leave food and drink outside the tour.
There is no parking on site, so plan how you will get to Delancey Place.

records.notes: Wheelchair is set to partial because the page describes only the south entrance as accessible. The programs page lists events from September 2026 to February 2027. The newest past event is October 4, 2026, and it is used as the sign of life. Volunteer guide applications are not counted in the rating. The visit page does not say whether there is an elevator.

records.name: Roxborough Church
records.summary: A church on Ridge Avenue with a 10:30 am Sunday service, children and youth programs, a preschool and after-school care, and a food pantry called The Table.
records.what_you_do: Attend the Sunday service and the fellowship lunch after it, join Roxy Kids (infant to grade 5), RUSH (grades 3 to 5) or ROX Youth (grades 6 to 12), or get food at The Table on Thursday mornings.

schedule.text: Sunday service at 10:30 am, in person and streamed on YouTube, followed by a fellowship lunch. The Table food pantry is open Thursdays from 10 am to noon. The site lists nursery, children's church, and youth groups with no set times.

first_step.how: Come to the 10:30 am Sunday service at 8230 Ridge Avenue, or fill in the Connect Card form on the church website.
first_step.basis: The visit page gives a service time, an address, a phone line and a Connect form, and describes a fellowship lunch after the service. It has no explicit welcome for first-time guests.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sunday worship starts at 10:30 am at 8230 Ridge Avenue, and the service is also streamed on YouTube if you want to watch first. A fellowship hour with lunch follows the service, a casual time to talk with others. The site does not give the service length, what to wear, or whether children's programs run during the service.
first_visit_tips: Plan to stay for the fellowship lunch that follows the service.
Call (215) 483-2762 or email office@roxboroughchurch.org about parking, entry, and children's programs, since the site does not describe them.
If you would rather watch first, the service is streamed on YouTube.

records.notes: The homepage shows only Hayride 2026 and a 2020 copyright, with no month. No last_sign_of_life is recorded, and the status is probably_active rather than active. The copyright year is not evidence. The Table pantry page publishes its own contact as Pantry@rpcnet.org and (215) 598-2016, and the church office is recorded as the group contact here. The pantry page names no eligibility or sign-up. The visit page is at /visit, since /visit-us returns not found. Kids and youth group days and hours are not published.

records.name: Roxborough Male Chorus
records.summary: A men's choral group in Northwest Philadelphia, founded in 1922, that gives two seasonal concerts a year and sings at veterans, church, and community events.
records.what_you_do: Sing in the chorus at its spring and Christmas concerts and at veterans, church, and community events. Ask about joining through the Contact Us link on the site.

schedule.text: Two seasonal concerts a year, a spring concert and a Christmas concert, plus performances at veterans, church, and community events. The site does not show rehearsal times.

first_step.how: Come to a spring or Christmas concert, or use the Contact Us link on the site to ask how to join.
first_step.basis: The FAQ says reading music is not required, but the site gives no way to join or audition, and the FAQ join answer is placeholder text, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: Most people first see the chorus at a concert, and the calendar lists its concerts at Ridge Avenue United Methodist Church. The site does not give ticket prices or rehearsal details, so use the Contact Us link to ask before you go.

records.notes: A WebSearch found only older third-party notices (WHYY and Patch, 2018 and 2019). They describe a chorus meeting at 8 pm at Leverington Presbyterian Church, 6301 Ridge Avenue, and open houses for prospective members. They are more than 24 months old, so they are not used as current facts. A 2019 notice also described declining membership. The calendar lists a September 11, 2026 event, a December 6, 2026 winter concert and a May 16, 2027 spring concert at Ridge Avenue United Methodist Church. The December 9, 2026 Masonic Village concert is private for residents and their guests. Partners and venues named on the site are listed as leads.
